study_identification.title: Neurodevelopmental model of schizophrenia revisited: similarity in individual deviation and idiosyncrasy from the normative model of whole-brain white matter tracts and shared brain-cognition covariation with ADHD and ASD

study_characteristics.study_objective: To investigate the similarity and differences in whole-brain white matter (WM) tract integrity among individuals with schizophrenia, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) by mapping individual deviations from normative ranges. The study also aimed to determine if shared dimensions of cognition and brain metrics exist across these diagnostic boundaries.

dataset_name.answer: Data collected at National Taiwan University Hospital

quality_checking_detail.answer: Rigorous quality control of MRI data was implemented by excluding those with low signal-noise ratio (SNR) or high signal-dropout counts (SDC), a proxy of in-scanner motion levels. As a result, SNR and SDC were comparable between these groups.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: All participants received MRI scans on the same 3-Tesla Siemens TIM Trio scanner with a 32-channel phased-array head coil.

modeling_method.answer: A moving average approach was used to obtain the unbiased mean and variance estimates for the GFA metric in each age range.

response_variable.answer: Generalized fractional anisotropy (GFA) of 45 major WM tracts

predictor_effects.answer: Sex-specific normative age models were constructed.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study used a single scanner, which eliminates site effects. Age and sex were explicitly modeled. Motion was controlled for during QC.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Spearman's correlation, unsupervised machine learning (Ward's hierarchical clustering and k-means clustering), and canonical correlation analysis (CCA).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study found that the patterns of white matter tract deviation and idiosyncrasy were similar between early-stage schizophrenia and neurodevelopmental disorders (ADHD and ASD), and this similarity decreased as schizophrenia progressed.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The similarity of deviance and idiosyncrasy of WM tracts between early-stage schizophrenia and ADHD or ASD, respectively, reduced as the disease progressed to subchronic or chronic schizophrenia. Using the WM deviation patterns as features, schizophrenia cannot be separated from neurodevelopmental disorders in the unsupervised machine learning algorithm. Moreover, schizophrenia, ADHD, and ASD shared linked cognitive dimensions driven by WM deviations.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The effect of psychotropic medications is unknown. The number of psychotic relapses was not considered. Some children with ADHD or ASD were under the common age of schizophrenia onset. Participants with intellectual disabilities were excluded.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Individual's WM deviations may contribute to diverse arrays of cognitive function along a continuum with phenotypic expressions from typical neurodevelopmental disorders to schizophrenia.

general_notes.general_notes: The study used a single-site harmonized cross-sectional MRI data.
